title: Slaying the infants of Babylon
source_text: Εἰ δὲ καὶ περὶ τοῦ καταφονεύειν δεῖ διηγήσασθαι ἅμα καὶ τὸ δυνατὸν τοῦ δικαίου περὶ πάντα, λεκτέον ὅτι φάσκων· „εἰς τὰς πρωΐας ἀπέκτεινον (πάντας) τοὺς ἁμαρτωλοὺς τῆς γῆς, τοῦ ἐξολοθρεῦσαι ἐκ πόλεως κυρίου πάντας τοὺς ἐργαζομένους τὴν ἀνομίαν“ γῆν μὲν τροπικῶς ἔλεγε τὴν σάρκα, ἧς „τὸ φρόνημα“ „ἔχθρα ἐστὶν εἰς θεὸν,“ πόλιν δὲ „κυρίου“ τὴν ἑαυτοῦ ψυχὴν, ἐν ᾗ ἦν „ναὸς θεοῦ,“ χωρήσας δόξαν καὶ ὑπόληψιν ὀρθὴν περὶ θεοῦ καὶ θαυμαζομένην ὑπὸ πάντων τῶν ὁρώντων αὐτήν. ἅμα οὖν ταῖς τοῦ ἡλίου „τῆς δικαιοσύνης“ αὐγαῖς ἐπιλαμπούσαις αὐτοῦ τῇ ψυχῇ ὡσπερεὶ δυναμούμενος υπ᾿ αὐτῶν καὶ κραταιούμενος ἀνῄρει πᾶν „τὸ φρόνημα τῆς σαρκὸς,“ λεγόμενον „ἁμαρτωλοὺς γῆς,“ καὶ ἐξωλόθρευεν ἀπὸ τῆς ἐν τῇ ψυχῇ ἑαυτοῦ „πόλεως κυρίου πάντας τοὺς ἐργαζομένους τὴν ἀνομίαν“ λογισμοὺς καὶ τὰ ἐχθρὰ τῇ ἀληθείᾳ ἐνθυμήματα. οὕτως δὲ καὶ ἀναιροῦσιν οἱ δίκαιοι πᾶσαν τὴν τῶν πολεμίων καὶ ἀπὸ κακίας ἐρχομένων „ζωγρίαν,“ ὡς μηδὲ νήπιον καὶ ἄρτι ὑποφυόμενον κακὸν καταλείπεσθαι. ἡμεῖς οὕτως ἀκούομεν καὶ τοῦ ἐν ἑκατοστῷ καὶ τριακοστῷ καὶ ἕκτῳ ψαλμῷ ῥητοῦ, οὕτως ἔχοντος· „θυγάτηρ Βαβυλῶνος ἡ ταλαίπωρος, μακάριος, ὃς ἀνταποδώσει σοι τὸ ἀνταπόδομά σου, ὃ ἀνταπέδωκας ἡμῖν· μακάριος, ὃς κρατήσει καὶ ἐδαφιεῖ τὰ νήπιά σου πρὸς τὴν πέτραν.“ „νήπια“ γὰρ „Βαβυλῶνος,“ ἑρμηνευομένης συγχύσεως, οἱ ἄρτι ὑποφυόμενοι καὶ ἀνατέλλοντες ἐν τῇ ψυχῇ εἰσιν συγχυτικοὶ λογισμοὶ οἱ ἀπὸ κακίας· ὧν ὁ κρατῶν, ὡς καὶ τῷ στερεῷ καὶ εὐτόνῳ τοῦ λόγου προσρῆξαι αὐτῶν τὰς κεφαλὰς, ἐδαφίζει „τὰ νήπια“ τῆς „Βαβυλῶνος“ „πρὸς τὴν πέτραν,“ γινόμενος διὰ τοῦτο „μακάριος.“ ἡβηδὸν οὖν τὰ τῆς κακίας καὶ παγγενεὶ κτείνειν κελευέτω ὁ θεὸς, οὐδὲν ἐναντίον διδάσκων οἷς Ἰησοῦς κατήγγειλε, καὶ ἐν ὀφθαλμοῖς τῶν „ἐν κρυπτῷ“ Ἰουδαίων ποιείτω ὁ θεὸς τὴν τῶν πολεμίων καὶ πάντων τῶν ἀπὸ κακίας ἀναίρεσιν. καὶ τοιοῦτόν γε ἔστω τὸ τοὺς μὴ πειθομένους νόμῳ καὶ λόγῳ θεοῦ, ὁμοιωθέντας τοῖς πολεμίοις καὶ ποιωθέντας ἀπὸ τῆς κακίας, πάσχειν ταῦτα, ἅπερ ἄξιον πάσχειν τοὺς ἀποστάντας λόγων θεοῦ.
pass_a_gloss: If also about slaughtering (καταφονεύω) it is necessary to narrate (διηγέομαι), together with the capability (τὸ δυνατόν) of the just man concerning all things, it must be said that, saying 'in the mornings I killed all the sinners of the earth, to destroy utterly (ἐξολοθρεύω) from the city of the Lord all those working lawlessness', by earth (γῆ) he spoke figuratively (τροπικῶς) of the flesh (σάρξ), whose mind-set (φρόνημα) is enmity (ἔχθρα) toward God, and by city (πόλις) of the Lord his own soul, in which was a temple (ναός) of God, having made room for/received (χωρέω) opinion (δόξα) and conception (ὑπόληψις) right (ὀρθή) about God and admired (θαυμάζω) by all who see it. Together then with the rays (αὐγαί) of the sun (ἥλιος) of righteousness shining upon (ἐπιλάμπω) his soul, as if empowered (δυναμόω) by them and strengthened (κραταιόω), he slew (ἀναιρέω) every mind-set of the flesh, called sinners of the earth, and utterly destroyed from the city of the Lord in his own soul all the reasonings (λογισμοί) working lawlessness and the thoughts (ἐνθυμήματα) hostile to the truth. Thus also the just slay all the captive-alive remnant (ζωγρία) of the enemies, also coming from wickedness (κακία), so that not even an infant (νήπιον) and just-sprouting (ὑποφύομαι) evil is left. We so hear also the text (ῥητόν) in the one hundred thirty-sixth psalm, holding thus: 'daughter of Babylon the wretched (ταλαίπωρος), blessed (μακάριος) the one who will repay (ἀνταποδίδωμι) you your recompense (ἀνταπόδομα), which you repaid us; blessed the one who will seize (κρατέω) and dash (ἐδαφίζω) your infants against the rock (πέτρα)'. For infants of Babylon, interpreted (ἑρμηνεύω) confusion (σύγχυσις), are the reasonings just sprouting and rising (ἀνατέλλω) in the soul, confusing (συγχυτικός), the ones from wickedness; of which the one seizing [them], so as to dash (προσρήγνυμι) their heads against the firm (στερεός) and vigorous (εὔτονος) [quality] of the word/reason (λόγος), dashes the infants of Babylon against the rock, becoming through this blessed. To the last youth (ἡβηδόν) then and with the whole race (παγγενεί) let God command (κελεύω) to kill (κτείνω) the things of wickedness, teaching nothing contrary to what Jesus proclaimed (καταγγέλλω), and in the eyes of the Jews in secret (ἐν κρυπτῷ) let God make the slaying (ἀναίρεσις) of the enemies and all those from wickedness. And let such be the [saying] that those not obeying (πείθομαι) the law and word of God, made like (ὁμοιόω) to the enemies and qualified (ποιόω) by wickedness, suffer these things, which it is worthy for those who have stood away (ἀφίσταμαι) from the words of God to suffer.
pass_b_english: And if we must also explain the slaughtering, and with it the righteous man’s power in all things, we must say that when he says, “In the mornings I killed all the sinners of the earth, to destroy from the city of the Lord all who work lawlessness” (Psalm 101:8), by “earth” he meant figuratively the flesh, whose “mind” “is enmity against God” (Romans 8:7), and by the city “of the Lord” his own soul, in which there was “a temple of God” (1 Corinthians 3:16), since he had received a right opinion and conception of God, one admired by all who saw it.

So at the moment when the rays of the sun “of righteousness” (Malachi 4:2) shone upon his soul, as though empowered and strengthened by them, he slew every “mind of the flesh” (Romans 8:7), which is called “sinners of the earth”, and destroyed from “the city of the Lord” within his own soul all the thoughts “that work lawlessness” and the notions hostile to the truth. In this way too the righteous destroy every living remnant (Deuteronomy 2:34) of the enemies, the ones that come from wickedness, so that not even an infant evil, just beginning to sprout, is left.

So too we understand the text in the hundred and thirty-sixth psalm, which runs thus: “O wretched daughter of Babylon, blessed is he who will repay you the recompense with which you repaid us; blessed is he who will seize your infants and dash them against the rock” (Psalm 137:8–9). For the “infants of Babylon”, a name that is interpreted “confusion”, are the confusing thoughts arising from wickedness that have just sprung up and are rising in the soul. The man who seizes them, so as to break their heads against the firmness and strength of the word, dashes “the infants” of “Babylon” “against the rock”, and for this reason becomes “blessed”.

Let God, then, command that the things of wickedness be slain “young and old” and “along with their whole race”; in this he teaches nothing contrary to what Jesus proclaimed. And let God bring about, “before the eyes” of those who are Jews “in secret” (Romans 2:29), the destruction of the enemies and of all that comes from wickedness. And let this be what is meant by saying that those who do not obey the law and word of God, having become like the enemies and been shaped by wickedness, shall suffer these things, which those who have fallen away from the words of God deserve to suffer.

choices.choice: Editorial supplement (πάντας) in the psalm quotation followed. LXX renumbering: Psalm 100:8 LXX = Psalm 101:8 English; Origen’s ‘hundred and thirty-sixth psalm’ is LXX Psalm 136:8–9 = Psalm 137:8–9 English, and Origen’s numbering is kept in the text with the English citation beside it. ‘Sun of righteousness’ is Malachi 3:20 in LXX and Hebrew = Malachi 4:2 in English Bibles. ἅμα ... ταῖς αὐγαῖς (‘together with the rays’) rendered ‘at the moment when the rays ... shone’, since Origen is reading the psalm’s ‘in the mornings’. Romans 8:7: τὸ φρόνημα τῆς σαρκὸς ἔχθρα εἰς θεόν rendered ‘the mind of the flesh ... is enmity against God’. 1 Corinthians 3:16 (‘you are a temple of God’), applied to the individual soul. ζωγρία (‘those taken alive’) points back to Deuteronomy 2:34 quoted in 7.19; rendered ‘every living remnant’. ‘Babylon ... interpreted confusion’ is the traditional etymology from Babel (Genesis 11:9); not cited inline since it is an etymology, not a quotation. ‘The rock’ and ‘the word’ are not explicitly identified with Christ here; λόγος in ‘the firmness and strength of the word’ kept lowercase (reason or the word of God), though a reference to the divine Word is possible. ‘Young and old’, ‘along with their whole race’ and ‘before the eyes’ are Celsus’s words from 7.18 turned back on him, so they stand in quotation marks; ‘Jews in secret’ is Romans 2:29. ‘Those who have fallen away’ renders τοὺς ἀποστάντας (literally ‘those who stood away’). χωρήσας (masculine) makes the psalmist, not his soul, the one who received the right opinion of God; θαυμαζομένην agrees with that opinion. ποιωθέντας ἀπὸ τῆς κακίας rendered ‘shaped by wickedness’. Origen’s psalm number (‘hundred and thirty-sixth’, LXX) is kept in the running text as his own words, with the English numbering in the citation.
agency: χωρήσας is masculine, so 'since it [the soul] had received a right opinion' -> 'since he had received a right opinion ... one admired by all who saw it'
'of the enemies, who come from wickedness' -> 'of the enemies, the ones that come from wickedness'
quoted Celsus words updated to match 7.18: 'young and old', 'along with their whole race'
ποιωθέντας: 'having taken their character from wickedness' -> 'been shaped by wickedness'
citations checked: Psalm 101:8 (LXX 100:8), Romans 8:7, 1 Corinthians 3:16, Malachi 4:2 (LXX 3:20), Deuteronomy 2:34, Psalm 137:8-9 (LXX 136:8-9), Romans 2:29
